purpose: decide whether the word 'certified' is defensible in the method name, given the evidence standard of each guarantee family

candidate_terms_examined.term: calibrated confidence bound on predicted gain (A)
candidate_terms_examined.what_it_would_mean: a well-calibrated predictive interval / lower confidence bound on DeltaQ
candidate_terms_examined.evidence_required: calibration diagnostics (coverage vs nominal) on held-out data; no distribution-free claim
candidate_terms_examined.achievable_now: YES, in principle, but not yet demonstrated; Phase 22 shows the GT-free proxies are near-chance, so calibration is unproven

candidate_terms_examined.what_it_would_mean: distribution-free finite-sample coverage of a prediction interval for DeltaQ
candidate_terms_examined.evidence_required: exchangeability assumption, a calibration set, explicit coverage/size trade-off
candidate_terms_examined.achievable_now: NO — requires a conformal construction and an exchangeability argument that do not exist yet; the refinement/ROI rules break naive exchangeability

candidate_terms_examined.what_it_would_mean: the gate meets a pre-declared risk target on held-out data
candidate_terms_examined.evidence_required: a held-out, non-inspected evaluation population and a pre-declared risk level
candidate_terms_examined.achievable_now: NO — Phase 22's policies were all evaluated on the population they were inspected on (post-hoc, optimistic). No held-out protocol exists yet

candidate_terms_examined.what_it_would_mean: refine when p(DeltaQ > epsilon) exceeds a chosen threshold
candidate_terms_examined.evidence_required: only a fixed threshold; no guarantee claim
candidate_terms_examined.achievable_now: YES — this is a straightforward design choice, but it is NOT a certificate

semantic_risk: 'Certified' in the machine-learning literature implies a GUARANTEE (conformal coverage, risk control, safety certificate). Using it for an uncalibrated threshold would be a terminological overclaim and a likely reviewer objection.
recommendation_detail: Adopt 'benefit-aware' (or 'gain-gated') as the defensible descriptor for the gate. The word 'certified' must be DROPPED from any provisional method name until EITHER (a) a conformal/risk-control construction is completed and validated on held-out data, OR (b) calibration coverage is demonstrated. Phase 23 cannot certify anything; it only rules out the claim for now.
conditional_upgrade_path: If, in a later phase, a conformal or risk-controlled construction on held-out data demonstrates coverage, the term may be revisited (USE_CALIBRATED or USE_RISK_CONTROLLED). That is a Phase-24+ decision and is explicitly NOT authorized here.
reviewer_credibility_note: An unearned 'certified' is the single easiest way to have the contribution dismissed. 'Benefit-aware' is both accurate and defensible today.
